subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should authorized hook-agent calls be allowed to opt into resuming an existing stored session, and which key-prefix and agent-scope guarantees must that persistent mode enforce?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically bounded, but it deliberately changes whether external webhook input can enter prior agent context; that authorization boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve explicit persistent mode
options.body: Adopt the linked PR’s opt-in `sessionMode: "persistent"` direction, retain isolated-by-default behavior, and require focused authorization and regression proof.

options.title: Keep hooks permanently isolated
options.body: Clarify the API and documentation that hook runs cannot resume stored conversation state, leaving integrations to inject their own context.

options.title: Design a narrower session target contract
options.body: Define a distinct existing-session target or tighter namespace policy before accepting any persistent hook-session surface.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Adopt the linked PR’s opt-in `sessionMode: "persistent"` direction, retain isolated-by-default behavior, and require focused authorization and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review already framed the preferred backward-compatible direction and the relevant security constraints.
